articles.dek: A 1M-subscriber Korean critic tested 40 creams, from Daiso to Dior. The comment thread underneath is a lesson in how Koreans actually shop.

source.title: 2026 수분크림  1위는? 백화점부터 다이소까지 40여종 성분, 효과 비교 추천, 비추천 I Best Moisturizers by Directorpi

takeaway.why_korea: Director Pi (1.03M subscribers) buys every product herself, runs device measurements and a subscriber test panel, then publishes one ranked cream list each winter. Korean viewers treat the upload as a shopping deadline rather than a review — comments show people waiting for the video before buying, and ordering the barrier cream and the 5,000-won Daiso repair cream the same evening.
takeaway.best_for: Dry and dehydrated-oily skin, barrier damage from winter heating, and anyone weighing a luxury cream against a 20,000-won one.
takeaway.skip_if: Very oily or acne-prone skin — she flags the rich wrapping and night creams as makeup-pilling and breakout risks.

articles.caveat: The 5,000-won Daiso pick is a 5% panthenol ointment with a heavy occlusive base — acne-prone skin can break out from that much occlusion, so patch test before covering the face.
body: Every winter the same question runs through Korean skincare forums: is the cream you are paying 80,000 won for actually better than the one on the Daiso shelf for 5,000? Director Pi answers it the expensive way — she buys all 40 products herself, measures them on the same instruments, then has a subscriber panel score them blind. This year's list runs from a 195,000-won Dior jar to a 5,000-won Daiso tube, and the ranking is not ordered by price.

The two winners worth knowing are the ones that cost least to try. COSRX's ceramide moisturiser took the barrier category for being light enough to layer under makeup, and the Daiso Fusiderm SOS cream took the repair category on a 5% panthenol formula that commenters describe as a night-only rescue. Above them, the most-liked comment of all recommends AESTURA's ATOBARRIER365 as a decade-long staple for dry skin.

What the comment section adds is the part no ranking can: the habits and the hedging. One highly-liked commenter points out that no cream beats not scratching your face, and another admits she went to buy a moisturiser, saw the upload was due, and went home to wait for it. The most-liked comment of all says the humble moisturiser, not the serums, is the category that actually decides your skin — which is also the quiet thesis of the video.

articles.title: Are Korean Sunscreens Safer? What 48 Products Reveal About US Filters
articles.title_ko: (Eng) 2026 선크림 1위는?🥇48종 비교 추천 🔥더마, 무기, 유기, 톤업 최고의 제품은?  성분, 기기 측정 결과 I Best Sunscreens by Directorpi
articles.dek: Korea's most-watched sunscreen ranking filters out five UV filters that are still standard in American sunscreens — and the comments argue about what that proves.

source.title: (Eng) 2026 선크림 1위는?🥇48종 비교 추천 🔥더마, 무기, 유기, 톤업 최고의 제품은?  성분, 기기 측정 결과 I Best Sunscreens by Directorpi

takeaway.why_korea: Korean shoppers read a sunscreen's ingredient table the way Americans read a nutrition label, so the annual ranking is a 25-minute, 48-product document rather than a top-ten list. This year's video opened by naming five UV filters being restricted in the EU and flagged as reef-harmful — including avobenzone and octocrylene, the backbone of many US sunscreens — and closed with separate winners for mineral, chemical, hybrid and tone-up formulas. It also carries a paid-ad label added after upload, which the top comments noticed.
takeaway.best_for: Anyone buying K-beauty sunscreen abroad or from a US K-beauty retailer; there is a distinct winner for dry, oily, acne-prone and makeup-first skin.
takeaway.skip_if: You want one single best product. The picks are split by filter type and skin type, and the most-liked complaints are about exactly that complexity and about top picks from brands nobody has heard of.

comment_quotes.ko:
[2026년 06월 01일 공지 추가] 2026년 05월 21일 영상 업로드 이후, 일부 브랜드사에서 영상 사용 계약 요청이 와 일정 기간 브랜드사 제품이 노출된 구간 영상을 라이선스 계약을 통해 사용할 수 있도록 하였습니다. 이에 2026년 06월 01일, 유료 광고 표시가 없던 영상에 유료 광고 포함 표시를 추가하였습니다. 사용 기간이 끝나면, 유료 광고 포함 표시와 해당 글은 삭제됩니다.

comment_quotes.en: [Notice added 1 June 2026] After this video went up on 21 May 2026, some brands asked to license the segments where their products appear, so we have added a paid-promotion disclosure to a video that originally carried none.

comment_quotes.label: Paid-ad notice
comment_quotes.note: The channel's own pinned disclosure, 38 likes — the clearest document of how K-beauty review videos get retro-labelled.

articles.caveat: Several top picks are built on filters the FDA has not approved (Tinosorb S, Uvinul A Plus, Mexoryl SX), so they cannot legally be sold as US sunscreens. Importing one means the SPF on the box is a Korean test result, not an FDA one — and the zinc-only pick is the safer bet if you burn easily.
us_search_terms: Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun rice probiotics
numbuzin No 3 tone up beige sunscreen
Fucidin derma trouble zinc calming sunscreen
body: American sunscreen and Korean sunscreen are not the same product category wearing different packaging. The US regulates UV filters as drugs and has approved roughly a dozen, most of them decades old; Korea approves newer, photo-stable filters that also happen to feel lighter. Director Pi opens this 25-minute ranking by naming five filters that are being restricted in the EU and flagged as harmful to marine ecosystems — avobenzone, octocrylene, ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate among them — and notes that several famous Western sunscreens are built on exactly those.

She then sorts 48 products into mineral, chemical, hybrid and tone-up groups, and picks a winner in each. For most overseas buyers the useful ones are Beauty of Joseon's Relief Sun (18,000 won, the comfortable everyday chemical option that spreads evenly by hand) and numbuzin's No.3 tone-up, which sits somewhere between sunscreen and a sheer foundation. If your skin reacts to chemical filters, the Fucidin zinc formula is the sensitive-skin pick; if you are oily, the Innisfree no-sebum tone-up is the matte one.

The comments are worth reading precisely because they do not simply applaud. The two most-liked threads ask for eye-sting data and complain that every top pick is an unknown brand — the same objection a US reader will have, since none of these are stocked at a drugstore. A separate thread catches that the video was labelled as containing paid promotion a week after upload, which the channel explains in a pinned comment. Treat the ranking as a well-documented shortlist and check the filter list yourself before you import.

articles.title: What Does a Dermatologist Buy at Olive Young for Under $10?
articles.title_ko: "이게 만원대..?" 가성비 좋은 올리브영 필수템 5가지를 20년차 피부과 전문의가 알려드립니다
articles.dek: A 20-year dermatologist picks five Olive Young items with one verb each — erase, fill, cover, smooth, protect — and 1.75M viewers rebuild their routine around it.

source.title: "이게 만원대..?" 가성비 좋은 올리브영 필수템 5가지를 20년차 피부과 전문의가 알려드립니다

takeaway.why_korea: Olive Young sale weeks are a national shopping event, and dermatologist-run channels have become the trusted filter over influencer hauls. This video is built as five verbs rather than five products, so viewers can slot it into a routine they already have, and the top comment is a viewer's own five-item recap with 547 likes — the comment section writes the shopping list for everyone else.
takeaway.best_for: Beginners assembling a first five-step routine; dry, sensitive or combination skin; anyone retinol-curious who wants the gentlest entry.
takeaway.skip_if: You want actives at prescription strength. Everything here is deliberately mild, and the retinol pick is a low-strength starter.

products.why: Step one, 'erase': the cleansing oil that both the doctor and the top comment start with.

products.name_en: Torriden Dive-In Low Molecular Hyaluronic Ampoule
products.why: Step two, 'fill': hydrating layer the comments assign to dry skin, with Wellage for oily skin.
Step three, 'cover': the barrier cream he recommends for dry and reactive skin.
Step four, 'smooth': a low-strength retinol built as an entry point, buffered with a cream.

products.name_en: Round Lab Birch Juice Moisturizing Sunscreen
products.why: Step five, 'protect': organic-filter daily sunscreen — and the one product commenters push back on hardest.

sentiment.method: editorial review of 80 top comments, weighted by likes
sentiment.note: Trust in the doctor is high and the purchase intent is visible. The scepticism is aimed at one product (the cleansing oil) and at copy-paste promo comments pedalling unrelated ampoules.

comment_quotes.label: Ad spam
comment_quotes.note: Copy-paste promo comment from an account plugging an unrelated ampoule; several near-identical versions rank in the top 20. Real evidence of how ad spam colonises Korean comment sections.

articles.caveat: Two cautions from the comment section itself: the Ma:nyo cleansing oil is the product most often named as a breakout trigger, and commenters argue the Round Lab birch sunscreen stings the eyes — patch test both before committing. The retinol is a starter strength; do not stack it with acids or prescription tretinoin.
us_search_terms: Torriden Dive In hyaluronic acid ampoule
Round Lab birch juice moisturizing sunscreen
body: Most routine videos fail because they assume you are starting from nothing. This one is organised around five verbs — erase, fill, cover, smooth, protect — which is why 1.75 million people watched a dermatologist walk through five Olive Young products in seventeen minutes. Each step is one product, all of them pharmacy-adjacent and mild, and the cheapest sits in the 10,000-won range.

The five are Ma:nyo's cleansing oil, a hyaluronic ampoule (Torriden for dry skin, Wellage for oily), ZEROID's barrier cream, a low-strength Theralogic retinol buffered with a moisturiser, and Round Lab's birch-juice sunscreen. What makes the video useful is the order: the retinol comes after the barrier cream, which is the sequencing most English-language retinol content skips.

The comment section does two jobs at once. The most-liked comment is a viewer's own recap of all five products with a note on which ampoule suits which skin type — effectively a free table of contents with 547 likes. And threaded among the genuine questions are two kinds of noise worth learning to spot: copy-paste promo comments pushing an unrelated ampoule, and a real disagreement about the sunscreen step, where commenters say the birch formula stings their eyes. Read the thread as a correction layer, not a fan club.

takeaway.why_korea: Olive Young's sale calendar sets the rhythm of Korean beauty buying, and creators race to publish 'what I actually repurchase' lists on day one of the sale. This one works because it is framed against luxury counters — a shopper who normally buys department-store brands says the Olive Young picks beat them — and because the cart mixes skincare with makeup, so it reads like a real basket rather than a sponsorship list.

body: The interesting thing about this haul is the comparison it makes. She shops department-store counters normally and says so up front; the Olive Young basket is the test of whether a 20,000-won product does the same job as a 90,000-won one. Twelve items later, the answer is mostly yes — with skincare taking the top half and colour makeup taking the bottom.

The skincare half is a restock list rather than a discovery list: Bioderma's micellar water, Torriden's hyaluronic serum, La Roche-Posay B5 and Bioderma Cicabio as repair creams, Illiyoon's ceramide cream, and Rejuran toner pads. The makeup half is where the sale behaviour shows — Rom&nd's Juicy Lasting Tint, Clio's Kill Lash mascara, Lilybyred's water tint — the products Korean viewers buy in multiples when the discount opens.

What the comments reveal is how fast this converts. One of the top comments is a viewer who ordered the entire list through Olive Young's same-day delivery while the video was still playing. Another, the most-liked of all, is a precise complaint that Lilybyred's tint is missing a gasket in its cap — the kind of defect report that only a comment section of regular buyers produces.
